questions.q: ------- the shipment arrived late, the customer still accepted the order.
questions.why: 後ろが「主語＋動詞」の節なので接続詞が入る。逆接の Although が文意に合う。Despite は前置詞、However は副詞。

questions.q: The seminar will be postponed ------- the speaker recovers from his illness.
questions.why: 「回復するまで」の意味で節を導く until が適切。during と despite は前置詞で節を直接続けられない。

questions.q: ------- the demand was higher than expected, the factory extended its working hours.
questions.why: 後ろに節が続くので接続詞。「需要が高かったので」という理由を表す Because が正しい。

questions.q: Applicants must submit ------- a résumé or a portfolio, but not both.
questions.why: or と対になる相関表現は either X or Y。「どちらか一方」の意味が but not both と合う。

questions.q: We will begin the meeting ------- Ms. Lee arrives, so please be seated.
questions.why: 「Lee さんが到着したらすぐに」という時を表す接続詞句。ほかは文意か品詞が合わない。

questions.q: The report must be submitted ------- noon on Friday.
questions.why: 「〜までに（期限）」は by。until は動作の継続、during は期間を表す。

questions.q: ------- the renovation, the lobby will remain closed to visitors.
questions.why: 後ろが名詞 the renovation なので前置詞の During。While などは接続詞で節が必要。

questions.q: The seminar room is located ------- the library and the cafeteria.
questions.why: 2つの場所の「間」は between。among は3つ以上のものに使う。

questions.q: Employees may enter the laboratory only ------- written permission from the director.
questions.why: only と組み合わせて「書面の許可がある場合のみ」となる with が自然。without だと意味が逆になる。

questions.q: Mr. Chen is the engineer ------- designed the new bridge.
questions.why: 先行詞は人で、空所の後ろに主語がなく動詞が続くので主格の who。

questions.q: The firm hired a consultant ------- advice helped cut costs by 12 percent.
questions.why: 空所の後ろに名詞 advice が続き「その人の助言」となるので所有格の whose。

questions.q: Customers ------- orders exceed $200 will receive free shipping.
questions.why: 「注文額が200ドルを超える顧客」。名詞 orders を修飾する所有格の whose が入る。

questions.q: Not only ------- the new software reduce errors, but it also saves time.
questions.why: 否定の副詞句 Not only が文頭に出ると倒置が起こる。主語が単数なので does が入る。

questions.q: Rarely ------- such a large number of applications for a single position.
questions.why: Rarely が文頭にあるので疑問文と同じ語順（助動詞＋主語）に倒置する。

questions.q: Had the shipment arrived on time, we ------- the deadline.
questions.why: If を省略した倒置の仮定法過去完了。主節は would have ＋過去分詞。

questions.q: The company is known for its ------- service to corporate clients.
questions.why: 名詞 service を修飾する形容詞が必要。reliable は「信頼できる」。

questions.q: Ms. Dubois ------- revised the contract before sending it to the client.
questions.why: 動詞 revised を修飾するので副詞の carefully。

questions.q: The airline offers ------- priced tickets for early bookings.
questions.why: 過去分詞 priced を修飾するのは副詞。reasonably priced で「手頃な価格の」。

questions.q: All visitors are required ------- their badges at the entrance.
questions.why: be required to do の形。「バッジを見せることが求められる」。

questions.q: The manager suggested ------- the meeting until next week.
questions.why: suggest は動名詞を目的語にとる動詞。to 不定詞は続けられない。

questions.q: The hotel offers a ------- breakfast to all guests staying more than two nights.
questions.why: complimentary は「無料の」。宿泊客への特典として自然。

questions.q: Ms. Han was ------- for organizing the annual charity event.
questions.why: be responsible for で「〜を担当している」。ほかの語は for と結びつかない。

questions.q: The board will ------- the proposal at its next meeting.
questions.why: 目的語 the proposal をとり「検討する」の意味になるのは consider。

questions.q: Sales of electric vehicles have increased ------- over the past five years.
questions.why: increase を修飾して「大幅に」を表す副詞は substantially。

questions.q: The software update is ------- with all major operating systems.
questions.why: be compatible with で「〜と互換性がある」。

questions.q: Please ------- the enclosed form and return it by April 5.
questions.why: form を目的語にして「記入する」の意味になるのは complete。

questions.q: The company's new policy aims to ------- employee turnover.
questions.why: 「離職率を下げる」という目的に合う動詞は reduce。

questions.q: Due to a scheduling -------, the workshop has been moved to Room 3.
questions.why: scheduling conflict で「日程の重複」。会場変更の理由として自然。

questions.q: The restaurant is famous for its ------- use of local ingredients.
questions.why: use を修飾して「革新的な」。ほかは意味が合わない。

questions.q: Mr. Park was ------- to the position of regional manager last month.
questions.why: be promoted to〜で「〜に昇進する」。
後ろに「主語＋動詞」が続くので接続詞。「作業中は」の意味の While が入る。
「道路に駐車する」は park on the street。

questions.why: 南駐車場や路上の利用を勧めた直後なので、その空き状況を説明する文が自然。

主語が reports（報告書）なので受動態。「提出されなければならない」。

c: New employees should complete the safety training.

questions.why: 領収書の添付ルールの直後なので、添付がない場合の扱いを述べる文が自然。

CITY TO EXTEND BUS SERVICE

Dunmore (June 2) — The Dunmore Transit Authority announced yesterday that it will extend Route 14 to the new Lakeside Business Park starting August 1. The route, which currently ends at Central Station, has been the subject of requests from workers at the park, where more than 2,000 people are employed. "Many of them currently rely on cars because there is no direct service," said Authority spokesperson Elena Brandt.

To pay for the extension, the Authority will reduce the frequency of Route 22 during the late evening. Buses on Route 14 will run every 15 minutes during rush hours and every 30 minutes at other times. Ms. Brandt added that a public meeting will be held on June 20 to collect residents' opinions on the new schedule.

LIBRARY TO REDUCE HOURS
Calder Daily, November 18

The Calder Public Library announced that it will reduce its weekday hours beginning in January. From Monday through Thursday, the library will close at 6 P.M. instead of 8 P.M. Library director Samuel Ibarra explained that the change is due to an 8 percent budget reduction approved by the city council in October. Saturday hours will remain unchanged.

Mr. Ibarra said the library will use the savings to continue its popular children's reading program and to purchase additional digital books. "We understand that this decision will inconvenience some patrons," he said, "but we hope to restore the evening hours when funding allows."

docs.label: Letter to the editor
docs.text:
To the Editor:

I was disappointed to read about the library's decision to close earlier. As a nurse who works until 5:30 P.M., I rely on the evening hours to borrow books and use the computers. Although I support the reading program, I believe the library could find savings elsewhere, for example by delaying the purchase of new digital books. I urge the council to reconsider or, at the very least, to keep one evening open until 8 P.M.

Rosa Delgado
